name: CT-996
lead: CT-996 is an investigational oral small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist from Roche, also registered under the code RO7795081 and the name tifeglipron.[2][3] Small-molecule oral GLP-1 agonists are a class designed to avoid the injection requirement of peptide drugs.[1]
Published results for CT-996 were not found; the evidence is limited to clinical trial registrations covering phase 1 and phase 2 studies.

paras: A phase 1 study in overweight or obese participants and people with type 2 diabetes enrolled 94 people from 2023.[2] A phase 2 study of daily oral tifeglipron in 352 people with obesity or overweight and a weight-related comorbidity has completed, and a 330-person phase 2 study compares doses with placebo or semaglutide in type 2 diabetes.[3][4] No results were found in the sources reviewed.

card.summary: Roche's experimental oral GLP-1 pill, with registered phase 2 trials and no results seen yet.
card.note: Investigational; no published efficacy data found.

quick.overview:
CT-996 (tifeglipron) is an experimental oral GLP-1 agonist from Roche for obesity and type 2 diabetes.

Phase 2 trials are registered; results were not found.
quick.mechanism: A small-molecule agonist of the GLP-1 receptor taken by mouth, rather than a peptide injection.
quick.risks: No published safety or efficacy data were found. Not approved.
